title: SecurityClaims
description: Out-of-process identity and authorization claim set. This schema defines claim NAMES and constraints only - possession of a claim set is not authentication; verification (signature, audience check, expiry) is the receiving adapter's responsibility (plan step7). iss and aud are identities: aud MUST bind the claims to one target backend service so tokens cannot be replayed across services. sub is the caller's workload identity - never a human principal and never a platform administrator. exp is an RFC3339 UTC timestamp; claims MUST be short-lived (the upper bound is a normative binding-document constraint, not asserted by this schema). Identity NEVER comes from the request body: self-asserted role or admin fields in a request body MUST be ignored by receivers.

aud.description: Audience: the target backend service identity. Missing aud would allow cross-service token replay.

sub.description: Subject: the caller's workload identity. A workload proves its deployment instance; it does not inherit human or platform-administrator rights.
